title: Be CIM or Be Memory: A Dual-mode-aware DNN Compiler for CIM Accelerators
problem: CIM accelerators can dynamically switch between compute mode and memory mode, but existing DNN compilers ignore this capability and statically assign resources, leaving performance on the table especially for LLMs with diverse memory and compute demands. No existing compilation framework models or optimizes the compute-memory mode switch in CIM hardware.
motivation: Emerging LLMs have highly variable memory and compute requirements across layers, and exploiting CIM's mode-switching capability is crucial to fully utilize CIM accelerator potential for real-world DNN workloads.
method: CMSwitch tells the compiler about a hardware capability it previously ignored: CIM accelerators can switch between compute mode (performing calculations) and memory mode (storing or accessing data). The compiler uses optimization techniques—dynamic programming (trying different solutions systematically) and mixed-integer programming (math for finding the best outcome when some variables must be whole numbers)—to determine where to split the network and how much hardware resources to allocate to compute versus memory modes. The result is packaged in a form that works across different CIM hardware targets.
key_novelty: It's the first compiler to jointly optimize compute and memory mode resource allocation using dynamic programming and mixed-integer programming, adapting resources dynamically to each neural network layer's requirements.
contributions: Novel hardware abstraction attribute exposing CIM mode-switching to the compiler optimization space
Compilation optimization pass combining dynamic programming and mixed-integer programming for optimal mode and resource allocation
Tailored meta-operator enabling generalized, hardware-agnostic expression of compiled CIM results
Average 1.31x speedup over state-of-the-art CIM compilation methods across diverse DNN workloads including LLMs
limitations: Not discussed; baseline CIM compilers are not named in the abstract.
primary_theme: CIM compiler with adaptive compute-memory mode switching
